title: The Story of Hong Gildong

subtitle.text: Once upon a time, there lived a boy named Hong Gildong.
He was the son of Lord Hong, a rich and powerful official.
One day while Gildong was reading, he heard servants whispering about him.
"Why does that boy bother reading so much?" one servant said.
"His father is a noble.
But his late mother was a servant.
That makes him lowborn."
"Yes," another said.
"He can never become a high official like his father.
The law of the land prevents it."
"He's even stronger than a grown man," the first servant said.
"But he can't become a military leader either."
Gildong had heard enough.
He jumped to his feet and lifted a heavy chest.
Bam! It made a loud sound as he slammed it down.
The servants rushed away.
"That will stop them from talking about me like that," he thought.
*** Later Gildong spotted his father
outside. As Gildong approached, Lord Hong thought of a dream he once
had. Lord Hong stood by a river in a beautiful, misty
valley. It was the land of the
gods. Suddenly the calm river started to
churn. The entire valley
rumbled. A splendid blue dragon rose from the water and flew toward him.
Though the dream was old, it was still vivid.
"Father—I mean, Your Lordship," Gildong said.
Gildong's voice shook Lord Hong out of the dream.
Lord Hong frowned.
"You know you must not call me Father. What do you want?"
"Do you have any new books for me to read?" Gildong asked.
Lord Hong sighed.
"Gildong was born after my dream of a splendid dragon," he thought.
"It was a sign that he is a gifted child.
But nothing can change his low birth.
Though I love him, I cannot show too much kindness."
"What do you need books for?" Lord Hong snapped.
"You don't need to learn."
He stormed off.
Gildong looked down, holding back tears.
When he looked up, he saw his older half brother, Inhyun, laughing.
Inhyun pretended to be Lord Hong.
"What do you need books for? You don't need to learn."
Gildong scowled.
"You shouldn't mock His Lordship like that!
Maybe you need to learn."
"You can't talk to me like that!
I'm noble and you're lowborn!" Inhyun shouted.
He pushed Gildong hard, but Gildong didn't move.
Inhyun picked up a stick.
"You want to learn? I'll teach you a lesson, servant boy."
Inhyun swung the stick at Gildong.
In a flash Gildong grabbed Inhyun's arm.
He flipped Inhyun onto the ground.
"Ahh!" Inhyun cried.
Inhyun's mother, Lady Yoo, rushed out.
"He beat me with a stick!
And he threw me across the yard!" Inhyun said between sobs.
"He's lying," Gildong said.
" He tried to beat me with a
stick." Lady Yoo narrowed her
eyes. "How dare you hurt my son!
I'll tell my husband about this.
He'll make you pay for it."
She grabbed Inhyun's hand and they walked away.
Gildong sighed.
"These two will get me in more trouble with Lord Hong!"
*** For three days and nights, Gildong had to stay in his
room. By the third day of his punishment, he was
bored. Late that night he sneaked
outside. He climbed a tree and looked up at the
moon. "Would things be better if Mother was alive?" he
thought. "I feel so alone in this
house." In the moonlight Gildong saw something moving
below. It was Lord
Hong. "Why are you out here, Gildong?" he
asked. Gildong said
nothing. "Speak," Lord Hong
said. "Why can't I call you Father?" Gildong blurted
out. Tears ran down his
cheeks. Lord Hong
sighed. "It is the law of the land. You know that."
"Why is it the law of the land? It's cruel," Gildong said.
"The law makes me an outcast in this house."
"Stop speaking nonsense," Lord Hong said.
"You're not the only lowborn child of a noble.
You must accept your position."
Gildong knew he shouldn't say more.
But he couldn't stop himself.
"What if I can't accept it?"
"Enough. Your punishment isn't over.
Get back to your room," Lord Hong said.
Gildong jumped down and obeyed.
*** One day Gildong met a new servant named
Mongdol. Mongdol looked closely at Gildong's
face. "Tee-hee-hee. You're Gildong, the servant's
son!" "I'm not a servant. My mother was," Gildong
said. Mongdol
grinned. "There's nothing wrong with being a
servant." Gildong was
surprised. Most of the servants ignored him or talked behind his back.
This one seemed friendly and curious.
"I'm all alone in this house because of my birth," Gildong said.
"Tee-hee-hee. I'll be your friend," Mongdol said.
"My friend?" Gildong had never had a friend before.
"Everyone says you're very strong.
Want to arm-wrestle?" Mongdol asked.
"Sure," Gildong said.
The two arm-wrestled, but neither won.
"You are very strong indeed," Mongdol said.
Gildong grinned. "Let's wrestle again!"
Gildong found Mongdol one afternoon.
Mongdol had just finished his work.
"Want to play?" Gildong said.
"Sure," Mongdol said.
They went out with a wooden board.
Gildong stood on one end.
Mongdol was about to jump on the other.
Just then Inhyun stomped over.
"Out of my way," he growled, shoving Gildong away.
He looked at Mongdol on the other side of the board. "Jump, servant!"
"Tee-hee-hee. Yes, young master."
Mongdol leaped high into the air.
Then— bam! He slammed down on the
board. Inhyun flew straight up into the tree branches.
"Ahh!" "Master Inhyun, please come down," Mongdol said. "Tee-hee-hee."
Inhyun kicked his legs wildly. Crack!
A branch broke, and Inhyun tumbled out of the tree.
"My leg!" he screamed in pain.
Lady Yoo rushed out.
"You're in big trouble!" she snapped at Gildong.
*** Later Gildong crept outside Inhyun's
room. He peered between the
doors. "Husband, look at our precious son's leg," Lady Yoo
said. "It's Gildong's fault," Inhyun
said. "He and that dumb servant tried to kill
me." Lord Hong frowned. "That doesn't sound like
Gildong." "Phew," Gildong thought. "Lord Hong trusts me at
least." He watched Lord Hong pace back and
forth. "But it's true, Father! It's true!" Inhyun
said. "Gildong and that servant are
trouble. You must punish them," Lady Yoo
said. Lord Hong sighed. "Fine. I'll send Mongdol
away." "My only friend," Gildong thought. His heart
sank. He hurried to the servants' quarters to warn
Mongdol. But Mongdol wasn't
there. Gildong looked
everywhere. "Tee-hee-hee." A laugh came from the
gate. "Mongdol!" Gildong ran over. "Did you hear the
news?" "I did not hear. Yet I already
know." "Huh?" Gildong was
confused. But Mongdol often said confusing
things. Gildong hung his head. "I guess this is
good-bye." Mongdol grinned. "No. We'll meet again soon. Tee-hee-hee."
He went through the gate and disappeared down the road.
"I'm all alone again," Gildong thought.
He looked down and kicked a stone.
A glimmer caught his eye. "What's this?"
Gildong saw a thin silver thread, like a spider's web.
The long thread led off in the direction that Mongdol went.
Gildong began to follow it.
The thread seemed to go on forever.
Gildong ran fast and far.
He leaped on tree branches and jumped over a stream.
Eventually he found himself high in the mountains.
Suddenly the thread disappeared.
"How strange," Gildong thought. "I wonder what that was."
Lady Yoo was scowling when her maid brought tea.
"My husband loves Gildong too much!" she said angrily.
"He should love Inhyun more—not some lowborn boy."
The maid nodded.
"My lady, perhaps you need to get rid of Gildong."
Lady Yoo sighed.
"I tried, but my husband sent only Mongdol away."
"Well, there are other ways," the maid said.
"But they are not cheap."
"I'll do anything. I just want him gone," Lady Yoo said.
"Of course, my lady." The maid smiled.
"I know someone who could help."
A few days later, Lady Yoo was walking with Lord Hong.
Her maid approached with a strange woman.
"My lord, my lady.
This visitor is here to speak to you," the maid said.
"Who are you?" Lord Hong asked.
The woman smiled. "My name is Choonja.
I am a face-reader.
I can also tell a person's future by looking at their face.
I am here to offer my services to Your Lordship."
Lord Hong grumbled. "I don't believe in such things."
"Husband, why not let her try?" Lady Yoo said.
"Fine," Lord Hong said.
Choonja stared at Lord Hong.
"Your Lordship has a most noble face.
You will serve the kingdom for many years."
She closed her eyes and waved her hands.
"I sense an energy from the side of your body . . . bamboo?"
Lord Hong blinked in surprise.
"I have a scar shaped like bamboo on my side.
How did you know that? Only my wife knows of it!"
Lady Yoo smiled at Choonja.
"You are very talented. Please tell us what you see in our son's face."
"Yes, and please read Gildong's face as well," Lord Hong said.
Inhyun came out first.
"This boy is kind and smart," the face-reader said.
"He will be an important man, just like his father."
Gildong came out next.
"You asked to see me, Your Lordship?" he said.
Choonja turned pale and backed away from the boy.
Lord Hong looked worried.
He sent both boys away.
"What did you see?" he asked Choonja.
"I cannot say it out loud, my lord," Choonja said.
"I command you to speak!" Lord Hong said.
Choonja crawled closer to Lord Hong.
"There is danger in the boy," she said quietly.
"What danger? Please tell us," Lady Yoo said.
"That boy will become a king!"
"Impossible!" Lord Hong said.
Lady Yoo grabbed his arm.
"Gildong is lowborn.
To become a king . . . he must commit evil deeds!"
"This is ridiculous!"
Lord Hong frowned at his wife and the face-reader.
"Gildong will never become a king.
Besides, the kingdom already has a king and plenty of heirs."
Choonja bowed her head.
"I only speak of what I see.
And Gildong's fortune puts you all in danger."
"If he causes any trouble, we'll all be punished," Lady Yoo said.
"Gildong could destroy this family.
You must do something, Husband."
Lord Hong looked at Choonja.
"Leave right now. And never speak a word of this to anyone."
Lord Hong went to his room.
He stayed there alone all night, thinking.
In the morning he summoned Gildong.
"You wanted to see me, Your Lordship?" Gildong asked.
"I'm sending you away," Lord Hong said flatly.
Gildong looked at him, surprised.
"Sending me away? Where? Why?"
"There is a cottage in the mountains," Lord Hong said.
"You must stay there and never leave.
A servant will bring your meals every day.
You can ask for anything you need.
But you may never return here again."
"Have I done something wrong, Your Lordship?
Why am I being punished again?" Gildong asked.
Tears filled his eyes.
Lord Hong looked down. "This is for your own good.
Good-bye, Gildong."
Life at the mountain cottage was boring for Gildong.
Every day a servant brought food and a book.
Gildong spent his days walking in circles in the yard.
He read and reread books.
"I was lonely before. Now I'm even more alone," he thought.
One day he saw a shimmer outside.
It was the silver thread again!
Gildong wasn't supposed to leave the cottage.
But he had to see where the thread led.
Quickly he began following it.
The thread led away from the cottage and deep into the woods.
Finally Gildong arrived at a cliff.
The silver thread went over the edge.
Gildong carefully crept closer.
As he did, his robe got caught on a tree branch.
He spun around, and suddenly the rock beneath him broke away.
"Ahh!" He was falling—fast!
Later that evening a servant came to Lord Hong.
"My Lord, Master Gildong was not at the cottage today.
When we searched the mountain, we found this by a cliff's edge."
The servant held out a piece of blue cloth.
Lord Hong took the cloth in his hands.
"This is from Gildong's robe," he said.
"We fear . . ." The servant bit his lip.
"Master Gildong is dead."
Gildong opened his eyes.
Mist rolled around him.
He was in a beautiful valley with high mountains.
He sat up, amazed.
"I'm on the back of a big turtle!"
The turtle was swimming in a wide, shining river.
Suddenly the turtle dove deep into the water.
Gildong grabbed the turtle's shell and held on tightly.
Soon the turtle reached a cave and entered it.
"What is this place?" Gildong thought, looking around.
He saw a red orb sticking out of the wall.
Gildong felt pulled toward the orb.
He grabbed the orb and held it.
"I've never seen this object before, but it feels familiar," he thought.
The turtle carried Gildong back to the surface.
"Tee-hee-hee." A familiar laugh rumbled through the valley.
Gildong knew that laugh.
He looked around and saw Mongdol.
He was huge and towered above the cliffs.
"I told you we'd meet again soon!" Mongdol said.
"Welcome back, Gildong."
Gildong was happy to see his friend.
But he was also confused. "I've been here before?"
"Yes!" Mongdol said.
"The thread of fate brought you home. You used to live here."
"That doesn't make any sense," Gildong said.
"This is the land of the gods," Mongdol said.
"Tee-hee-hee."
Gildong frowned. "Mongdol, this isn't funny. I don't understand."
Slowly Mongdol turned into an old man wearing a dazzling white robe.
"You lived here before as a blue dragon."
His voice sounded different too.
Poof! Mongdol appeared in front of Gildong in his normal size.
He pointed to the red orb.
"When you lived here, that was your treasure.
It's a wish jewel that contains the powers of Heaven and Earth."
Gildong blinked. "Why did I leave?
This place seems so peaceful and beautiful.
You know how lonely I am at home."
"You must find your destiny," Mongdol said.
"It's time to return to your world now.
Take the wish jewel with you.
Keep it with you always."
Gildong stared at the large orb.
"I'm supposed to carry this with me everywhere I go?
Look at the size of it.
Maybe if it was small like a—"
A blinding light flashed.
Now Gildong was holding a fan.
Mongdol grinned.
Gildong still didn't understand what was happening, but he nodded at Mongdol.
"How do I get back to my world?"
Mongdol pointed to the fan.
Gildong opened it.
Energy swirled around.
"Wow," Gildong said.
"Take me home!"
Lady Yoo sat with Inhyun.
They watched as servants prepared for Gildong's funeral.
"I'm glad the servant boy is dead," Inhyun said.
Lady Yoo patted him.
"Now your father will love you best."
Crack! Just then a bolt of lightning struck a tree.
When the smoke cleared, Gildong stood on top of the tree, holding a fan.
Everyone screamed.
"It's a ghost!" Inhyun cried, hiding behind his mother.
Lord Hong rushed outside. "Why is everyone screaming?"
He saw Gildong and gulped.
"Gildong's ghost has come for revenge.
I should not have sent him away."
Gildong scratched his head.
"What ghost? I'm not a ghost." He jumped down. Lord
Hong reached out and touched Gildong's robe. "You're alive?" "Of
course I am," Gildong said. "Everyone
said you fell from a cliff and died!" Lord Hong said. "I
fell from a cliff, but I didn't die," Gildong said. "I
just got back from the land of the gods." Lord
Hong was puzzled. "Poor
child, you must have hurt your head. But never mind that." He
turned to address everyone. "There
is no need for a funeral. Gildong
is home, and he shall stay here for good!" ***
In the morning Gildong went outside with his fan.
"It is time to learn how to use its magic," he thought.
He opened it. "Vortex!"
A gust of wind blew hard around him.
Gildong laughed. "Amazing!"
He practiced using the fan all morning.
Then Inhyun found him.
"Give me that!" Inhyun reached for the fan.
"Float!" Gildong rose into the air.
Inhyun gasped. "You must be a demon.
How can you do that?"
"Illusion!" Gildong cried.
A giant snake appeared and hissed angrily at Inhyun.
"Gildong is trying to kill me again!"
Inhyun ran away, screaming.
Poof! The snake disappeared.
Gildong smiled. "I wonder what else this fan can do." ***
Inhyun told his parents about Gildong's new powers.
Lord Hong laughed. "Inhyun, don't make up stories.
You should focus more on learning, like Gildong."
Lady Yoo was furious at hearing this.
She stormed to her room.
"What's wrong, my lady?" her maid asked.
Lady Yoo stomped her foot.
"I was happier when I thought the lowborn boy was dead!"
"What if the boy died for real?" her maid said.
"If you wish, I know someone who can help.
Teukjae is the perfect man for the job."
Lady Yoo's mouth twisted into a nasty smile. "Yes."
It was late at night.
Gildong was in his room, reading.
Suddenly he heard the flutter of a bird.
A crow landed just outside the doors. Caw! Caw! Caw!
The crow flew away.
"That's odd," Gildong said to himself.
"Crows don't usually cry at night.
Maybe it's trying to tell me something."
Shivers went down his spine.
Gildong had a bad feeling.
He saw his fan nearby and reached for it.
*** Teukjae peered at the
room. Gildong was reading in front of a
candle. "This will be easy," Teukjae
thought. Silently he leaped into the
room. But when he landed, Gildong was
gone! Before he could look for the boy, the room began to
shake. Teukjae found himself in a dark
forest. "This must be magic," Teukjae
thought. "I didn't know this boy was so
powerful. Luckily he cannot match my skills or
strength." The sound of a flute floated through the
forest. Teukjae heard the crunch of footsteps behind
him. He spun around, but no one was
there. When he turned back, he saw
Gildong. The boy was playing a flute and riding a
donkey. "Surrender now, and I'll let you go," Gildong
said. Teukjae laughed. "No one has ever fought me and lived.
And you're just a child! You'll never escape from me."
"Don't say I didn't warn you," Gildong said.
Teukjae reached for his daggers.
He threw them at Gildong.
Gildong jumped into the air and unfolded his fan. "Vortex!"
Whoosh! A strong wind blew the daggers away.
Then the daggers changed direction.
They were heading straight toward Teukjae.
Teukjae jumped away, but the ground wasn't there.
He was falling fast in the darkness.
"I surrender!" Teukjae cried.
"Why did you come for me?" Gildong's voice boomed around him.
"Lady Yoo sent me. Now will you let me go?" Teukjae said.
Bam! Teukjae crashed down onto the floor.
He was in the boy's room again.
Everything had been an illusion.
Gildong stood over Teukjae.
"I will let you go.
But you must never harm anyone ever again.
I'll come for you if you do."
Teukjae nodded and ran out of the room.
Gildong watched the man disappear into the darkness.
"I knew Lady Yoo hated me," Gildong thought.
"But I didn't think she'd send someone to kill me."
He bit his lip. "Lady Yoo will try to get rid of me again.
There's only one thing to do."
Gildong went to Lord Hong's room.
Lord Hong heard soft footsteps.
"Who's out there?" Lord Hong asked.
"Gildong."
Lord Hong opened the doors and saw Gildong wearing a hat.
"What are you doing here?
Why are you dressed like that?"
"I've come to say good-bye," Gildong said.
"What do you mean good-bye?" Lord Hong frowned.
"It is late. Go back to your room."
Gildong knelt down.
"I have decided to leave Your Lordship's house.
Tonight an evil man was sent to harm me."
"What? Who sent him?" Lord Hong asked.
Gildong thought for a moment.
The truth would break Lord Hong's heart.
"It doesn't matter," Gildong said.
"But it's not safe for me here.
Please don't worry about me.
Because I am lowborn, I cannot serve the king like you can.
I cannot call you Father.
I must go and find my own destiny."
Lord Hong looked troubled.
"I'm afraid it will not be easy.
But I won't stop you.
Never forget that you are my son.
And always remember to do good in the world."
"I will. Farewell, Your Lordship."
Gildong stood up and bowed.
Then he disappeared into the night, leaving his father—and his home.
For days Gildong wandered the country with nowhere to go.
He didn't know what would happen to him.
Eventually he came to the mountains.
He stopped on a high ridge and looked out.
"The world is so big.
And I'm all alone now," he thought.
"At least I have my fan."
Feeling tired, he decided to sleep.
A while later something stirred him awake.
He looked around but saw nothing unusual.
Gildong stood up and stretched.
"Oh no! My fan is gone!"
He saw a young girl far ahead on the path.
She had the fan.
"Hey! That's mine!" Gildong yelled.
The girl turned around.
"It's mine now! Thank you, little lord!"
She took off, running as fast as she could.
Gildong chased after her.
Racing like the wind, he nearly caught up to her.
The girl turned around, shocked. "You're fast!"
Gildong ran even faster. "Give me my fan!"
The girl darted behind a large rock.
When Gildong got there, she was gone.
"Ugh." Gildong groaned. "Where'd she go?"
He wandered around and found a cave.
"Maybe she went in here," he thought.
Gildong went inside.
The cave was long and dark.
At the back, light shone through a crack.
Gildong peered through the crack.
"Whoa!" he whispered.
There was a huge village hidden within the mountains!
Gildong felt the cave wall.
He realized it was a door.
He was about to open it when he heard voices.
He looked through the crack again.
"The fan thief!" he thought.
The girl was with a group of people.
"Uncle Mok, look at this pretty fan I stole!" she said.
"That fan is useless, Nabi," Mok said.
"Yeah, go steal something useful," another person said.
"We can toss the fan in the fire."
Hearing this, Gildong burst through the door.
"Give me my fan!" he shouted.
Nabi tossed the fan to Mok.
"See, the little lord really wants it back.
It must be valuable."
Gildong shook his fist at Mok.
"Give it back, or I'll fight you!"
Mok looked at the boy and let out a loud laugh.
Everyone else laughed too.
Gildong's face turned red.
"This is your last chance.
Give it back, or you'll be sorry!"
The group roared with laughter again.
"Grr." Gildong went over to a huge rock and picked it up.
The laughter stopped as he lifted it over his head.
He held it with one hand and glared at Mok.
"Now will you give my fan back?"
Mok tossed the fan to Gildong.
"Please don't harm us!"
Gildong set the rock down.
"Sorry I took it," Nabi said.
"Uncle Mok told me to steal something valuable.
And that was all you had when I found you, my lord."
"I'm not a lord," Gildong said.
"My father is a noble.
But my mother was a servant.
So that makes me a lowborn commoner."
Mok put his arm around Gildong.
"We're all commoners too.
We should stick together.
Why don't you join us?
You're strong. You can probably read and write.
Our group could use a smart guy like you."
"Join you? What do you do?" Gildong asked.
"We're just a humble group that sticks together," Mok said.
"We go out and take things from people when we need them."
Gildong blinked. "You mean you're thieves?"
"We only do it to survive!" Nabi said.
"Well . . ." Gildong thought for a moment.
He didn't want to stay with a group of thieves.
But he didn't have anywhere else to go.
"I guess I'll stay here for now."
The group cheered. "Hip-hip-hooray for—"
"What's your name?" Nabi asked.
"Hong Gildong."
Mok patted Gildong on the back.
"Tonight we will have a feast to welcome Hong Gildong!"
That night the group held a feast.
Everyone had a bowl of porridge.
Small dishes of vegetables sat on the table too.
"Welcome to our group of bandits!" Mok said.
The thieves cheered, then everyone started to eat.
Gildong looked at his bowl.
There was so little porridge.
"Is this really a feast ?" Gildong
said. Nabi nodded. "Of course it
is. This is more porridge than we normally
eat. And we have vegetables today." She
giggled. "You've got a lot to learn, little
lord." "I told you, I'm not a
lord. I'm a commoner, just like you," Gildong
said. "You grew up in a noble's house," Nabi said.
"So, you're not just like us.
This is how common people eat."
"Oh," Gildong said softly.
"We've got twenty sacks of rice," Mok said.
"But we need to save them so we don't run out."
"You're thieves. Can't you just steal more?" Gildong asked.
"Most people don't have much food," Nabi said.
"And lots of bad officials charge high taxes," Mok said.
"They take grain from the poor and keep it for themselves."
"Officials do that?" Gildong felt upset by what he was learning.
Greedy officials had more than they needed while people went hungry.
Mok nodded. "In fact, I heard about a temple in Hapcheon.
The greedy monks there have a storehouse filled with grain and treasure.
It's huge—I wish we could rob it!"
"Why can't you?" Gildong asked.
"It's impossible to rob," Mok said.
"There are too many monks there."
"Hmm." Gildong thought for a moment.
He wanted to learn more about these greedy monks.
An idea came to him. "I'll visit that temple."
*** Gildong waited at the temple gate with a few
followers. The head monk rushed out and
bowed. "I'm sorry to keep you waiting, young
master." He took a good look at Gildong.
"We are honored by your visit. What brings you here?"
"I am preparing for the royal examinations," Gildong said.
"I have heard good things about your temple.
I wish to study here."
The head monk nodded eagerly.
"Certainly, young master. Please be our honored guest.
Though, we must humbly ask for a donation."
"I will send twenty sacks of rice soon," Gildong said.
The monk's eyes lit up. "That's very generous of you."
"Prepare a feast for my return in a week.
All the monks must attend," Gildong said.
The monk bowed deeply. "As you wish, young master."
Gildong returned to the temple with a large party of servants.
The head monk was there to greet him.
"I've had a long journey.
I'm very hungry from my travels," Gildong said.
The head monk smiled. "We have prepared a feast for you."
"Good," Gildong said. "Please gather all the monks."
"Of course, young master," the monk said.
"Everything is exactly as you requested.
The monks in this temple are gathering right now."
The head monk took Gildong and his servants to a large pavilion.
Dishes of food filled the tables.
All the monks were gathered, waiting for Gildong.
The head monk led Gildong to the seat of honor.
"What a wonderful feast!" Gildong said.
"Let's eat and be merry!"
Everyone ate and drank.
The monks joked and laughed.
Gildong watched the party.
After a while the monks began to look tired.
"Now seems like a good time," he thought.
When no one was looking, Gildong reached into his sleeve.
He sprinkled some sand on his rice.
Then he put a spoonful into his mouth.
Crack!
All the monks stared at him.
"Ahh! Ouch! My teeth!" he cried loudly.

He laughed as he read it.

Gildong looked out across the sea.
"I think it's time for a new adventure.

"What?" Mok gulped.
"You can't go, boss. It's not safe."
"I'll be fine," Gildong said.
"I must see the king and end this once and for all."
He gathered everyone closer.
"Here is what you must do while I'm gone . . ."
